basis.governing_question: How should Seguros Atlântida's claims department be organized, roles and handoffs included?

sub_questions.question: How is the claims department organized today, with which roles and handoffs?
Where do the current structure, roles and handoffs hold claims work back?
Which target organization options for claims are worth comparing?
What roles and handoffs does the chosen target organization need in detail?
Which target organization for claims will the executive committee approve?

drivers.evidence: One claims department of about 140 people in Lisbon.

work.unit: Unit diagnosed (interviews, process walk-throughs, workload and cost baseline)

phase_work.why: One department diagnosed in a single pass of interviews, walk-throughs and baseline; start-up and synthesis weeks added.

work.unit: Target model for the whole organization (structure, roles, governance)
Unit-level design detailed with the unit's leaders

phase_work.why: Target model, then roles and handoffs detailed with unit leaders, then one sign-off cycle, which puts the max 1 week above typical.

sizing.levers: Running roles-and-handoffs design alongside the target model, and agreeing the executive committee review date upfront, would shorten Design most.

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Map how the claims department is organized today, including roles and handoffs, and find where the work breaks down.

gate.label: Priorities for design
gate.decision: Which diagnosed issues must the target organization solve first?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Define the target claims organization, with roles and handoffs, in a form the executive committee can approve.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Approve the target claims organization to take to the executive committee?

architect_notes: Length is an estimate; Design takes the middle of 7-11 weeks and reaches the top if the target model and sign-off run long.
The single claims department (about 140 people, Lisbon) comes from public research; the client must confirm it, as more units would add weeks.
The brief makes the executive committee the approver but lists only the COO and Head of Claims; confirm who sits at the final gate.
Departure from the archetype: Design carries no transition-plan unit, because the brief asks only for an approved target organization.
